# Developing Codex Relay

These instructions govern **owner-admitted Relay/Codex development**. The
[product user manual](packages/codex-relay/skill/references/workflow.md#owner-acceptance-and-execution-routes)
also defines owner acceptance and ordinary authorized standalone/manual work;
native admission and publication rules apply to the Relay route. Ordinary
human contributors use [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); they do not need
Task/Step admission, an installed Relay consumer or Codex UI tools to propose
a change.

## Shared governance and Relay routing

Relay explicitly adopts all eleven complete applicable Shared Governance **12.5.0**
protocols, accepted source `f51fd0ab22ff61fab48bd1e5af96918d77af1ec6`,
distribution `e19ceeaa3ffe608fe078d37171ddd7cd5a940dda`.
Read each complete topic when triggered; conditional loading excludes no clauses:

- [Context loading](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/context-loading.md): startup, complete relevant context and mutable refresh.
- [Task handoff](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/task-handoff.md): Task execution, results, acceptance and continuation.
- [Independent review](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/independent-review.md): substantive assessment, evidence, findings and rereview.
- [Contract/decision maintenance](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/contract-and-decision-maintenance.md): material operator changes, durable decisions and same-change guidance.
- [Proportional controls](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/proportional-controls.md): controls, operator cost and existing proof.
- [Requirement authority](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/requirement-authority.md): binding requirements versus engineering choices.
- [Package versioning](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/package-versioning.md): Relay Skill/package release and dependency lifecycle.
- [Producer self-adoption](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/self-adoption.md): Relay instruction, Skill and boot candidates.
- [GitHub repository governance](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.development-governance/12.5.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/github-repository-governance.md): workflow and protection decisions, including GH-014 for relevant optional settings choices.

For an already-admitted legacy operation, the live Issue body retains its original
canonical Task role under that operation's frozen source contract. Keep current
requirements, owner corrections, scope/boundary decisions and task status in
that body. Comments hold discussion, evidence, Outcomes, handoffs and history;

Apply Shared RA-007 to project context: this conversation acts for the declared

All human-readable GitHub publication for this repository is in English,

## Task identity and startup rename

Follow the canonical [manual result PR Step-label procedure](packages/codex-relay/skill/references/workflow.md#manual-result-pr-step-labels)
for manual Codex responsibility, Issue/admission consistency checks and the
shared Writer projection for validated manual results. Task #177 is included in
Task #199; the old manual-executor labeling workaround is superseded.

`Task N` is canonical GitHub Issue `#N`, not a separately allocated number.
A Task/Issue defines the authorized goal, boundaries, and completion/closure
intent. Shared TH-026 defines equivalent names for both closure modes. Qualified
Relay tooling requires the existing spellings. Canonical Task producers
must include exactly one explicit
`Issue closure policy: keep-open` or `Issue closure policy: close-authorized`
field in the live Issue body, using `close-authorized` only with owner authority.
CR producers preserve that Issue decision when updating canonical authority;
a CR does not independently authorize closure. Missing, malformed or conflicting
closure metadata prevents automatic closure with a visible warning; it is not
evidence of an owner-selected indefinite hold.
Author concrete completion/closure conditions beside that single field through
[Relay closure authoring](contracts/README.md#closure-policy-authoring), binding
TH-002/003/026 to trusted v4 Decisions. Use `close-authorized` for whole-Task
completion on the designated final merge or through the authorized no-PR
completion path. Before a guarded merge, owner continuation verifies completion
and native closing linkage. Use `keep-open` with a stated condition for
trusted continuation and a non-closing reference on any PR. Once that
preauthorized condition and all other obligations are verified,
trusted owner continuation closes without a policy-change Decision or another
discretionary permission prompt. Preserve explicit holds and old admitted terms. A native CR cannot change Task-wide closure authority. Retained v3 keeps
its original charter/Request rules; exact result acceptance and protected owner
continuation remain mandatory.
After an explicit `Authority model: github-native-v1` migration, the Issue is
the stable charter. In the current schema-v4 source contract, trusted Decisions
amend durable semantics and Writer creates the sole immutable
Step/profile/route/scope admission snapshot at execution. A new complete public
Request is unnecessary; ordinary comments remain selected evidence. Already
admitted schema-v3/legacy operations preserve their selected authority, Steps,
bodies and replay/recovery behavior through their frozen original runtime. Use the
[GitHub-native contract](contracts/README.md#github-native-task-authority) and
paired qualified Reviewer/controller. Source changes alone do not upgrade or
qualify an installation. Labels and bounded titles are projections,
not a second Step authority. The former owner metadata CLI and legacy Node
parsers are retired from the current product.
On a paired, qualified schema-v4 installation, fresh Task work or remediation
must use the current v4 authority path. An unmarked Task stops with an actionable
protocol mismatch; use current authority or an explicitly owner-authorized
migration before admission. Historical Requests provide no current execution
fields. A current decisive remediation CR must use schema v4, and fresh old-schema
authority publication is refused.
Safe completion, Outcome publication and recovery of an exact already-admitted
old attempt use its frozen original source and bindings. This is a
fresh-execution boundary, not a blanket support cutoff for older installations.
Fresh durable Decision/CR publication also uses current v4 authority;
exact reserved old publication recovery and old admitted-result acceptance remain
supported without creating a new old-schema governance chain.
Current authority may retain an exact trusted schema-v3 Decision as provenance
when later active v4 Decisions replace every effective field; existing evidence
needs no additional Decision or formal supersession. Still-effective unhandled
v3 semantics stop fresh admission with `CURRENT_PROTOCOL_REQUIRED`. Exact
admitted v4 results preserve their selected Decision references and body hashes.
Historical v3 Requests remain opaque and supply no current execution fields.
Shared TH-006–009 owns Step and thread semantics. Writer's execution-time
allocation below implements it; historical embedded Step descriptions supply
no future admission authority.

Use these complete titles, with a concise purpose:

- Implementation: `Task N — Step S — <purpose>`.
- Remediation: `Task N — Step S — CR-N-NNN — <CR purpose>`.

Preserve an exact title supplied by live task/CR authority, including an
explicit phase qualifier. Step is a positive, explicitly resolved value.
For a new schema-v4 execution, the owner applies the native
`codex-ready-auto` or `codex-ready-manual` command on the canonical target;
Writer verifies and consumes that event and allocates Step in protected
admission state. Charter creation, Decisions, CR publication and labels do not
allocate Step. At a genuinely new routed admission, Writer reads the canonical Issue's single
valid `step-N` position under its existing serialization lock and compares it
with successful durable admissions. The next Step is N+1; without a label it is
last admitted Step+1, or 1 when neither exists. An owner-maintained position
above Writer history permits standalone iterations. A position below successful
history, malformed/conflicting labels, overflow or a concurrent position change
fails with an actionable diagnostic. Rejected launches allocate no Step;
same-attempt replay/recovery retains its Step. The label supplies numbering,
never execution or admission authority. Writer projects the position only after
durable admission and verifies the native result.
Titles and `step-S` labels project admitted state.
Exact already-admitted schema-v3/legacy attempts keep the Step and metadata
checks of their frozen original source. Same-attempt replay or publication
repair changes no Step; approval does not increment it. New work uses current
v4 admission, without a successor Request or owner new-phase CLI. Read the
protected snapshot for current admitted identity; do not infer it from prose,
commits or the largest historical Step.
Missing or conflicting admission metadata needs reconciliation. Step labels
alone do not launch work or grant authority. The
[Issue template](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/codex-task.md) supplies
the authoring baseline; its creation is not admission or dispatch.

For an owner-launched manual session, rename the current Codex task at startup
to the exact title from the admitted snapshot/handoff. An exact old attempt
keeps the title supplied by its original admitted handoff. A backlog Decision or ready label alone
does not supply a future Step/title.
Use the native task-title tool once with only `title` (omit `threadId`); search
deferred tools if it is not initially visible. Recording the title only in a
prompt, PR or Outcome is insufficient. When the current native tool surface can
read back the persisted title, compare it with the exact requested title. A
successful rename call alone does not prove persisted state. Report the call
result and any read-back mismatch, truncation or unavailable verification
truthfully. An unavailable/failed rename or unverified exact title is
non-blocking; do not repeat the rename to chase a match. Preserve the supplied
Task/Step identity; never infer a new Step from history. Automatic runtime
execution already passes its resolved title to Codex and does not require a
worker to discover or invoke the UI rename tool.

## Canonical checkout and safe Git handoff

For repository changes assigned to Codex, Codex owns the implementation branch,
commit and PR flow. ChatGPT/owner orchestration must not create implementation
branches, commits or PRs unless the owner explicitly requests it. Automatic
workers still delegate GitHub publication to trusted Writer.

The canonical Task may authorize implementation continuation on an existing
task branch and its current PR when one exists through the current charter and
trusted Task Decisions resolved into the admission snapshot, as described in
the [controller contract](controller/README.md#issue-authorized-implementation-continuation).
This preserves Issue authority and implementation identity without a Reviewer
CR or its integration-merge permission. Replay/recovery of an admitted attempt
keeps Step; a genuinely new schema-v4 execution receives a fresh admitted Step.
Exact already-admitted old operations retain their original source, authority
and Step; they do not create a fresh legacy phase. Manual handoff retains its
full copyable prompt and visible
canonical identity/pointer; folding changes presentation only.

Before applying an existing PR's starting-head gate, read its live repository,
branch, base and required SHA. Inspect the current checkout, worktrees, dirty
state and unpublished commits. Safely fetch the canonical branch and switch
to it only when local work is preserved; a clean branch that only lags can be
fast-forwarded. Then compare both local canonical HEAD and refreshed remote
head with the required SHA. An incidental initial branch is not a mismatch.
Never reset, force-push, discard, absorb unrelated work or replace the branch/PR
to satisfy a gate. A real mismatch or unsafe unpublished work is a concrete
boundary. Trusted normalization applies before worker access; a model-modified
worker checkout must still use the trusted import boundary below.

Before any terminal result, including BLOCKED, reconcile task-owned changes
and preserve useful progress in substantive commits. Publish safe, authorized
unpushed task commits to the existing task branch; automatic workers hand them
to Writer. Leave unrelated changes untouched. Remove only confirmed disposable
residue; use ignores for repeatable generated artifacts without hiding work.
State wholly inside owned disposable TEST follows
[TEST Environment Authority](docs/execution-policy.md#test-environment-authority);
cleanup there does not require individual-file ownership proof or preservation
of disposable state. Preserve useful product-source work and ordinary
worker/Writer collection and publication evidence.
If a safe commit/push or clean handoff is impossible, report exactly what stays
local and the authority, branch, permission or security boundary. Never create
empty or metadata-only commits merely to record status. Explain material
execution warnings even when the result is green.

## Execution context and shells

Identify the actual execution environment and use the shortest qualified
transport that preserves the admitted implementation and authority boundary.
Read the detailed [execution environment and shell routing](CONTRIBUTING.md#execution-environment-and-shell-routing)
rules just in time when command routing, WSL/native-filesystem behavior or
PowerShell/native failure propagation matters. A transport choice grants no
additional credential or production authority. Protected operations outside
disposable TEST retain their source-controlled entrypoints; shell and tool
choice inside its sandbox follows
[TEST Environment Authority](docs/execution-policy.md#test-environment-authority).

For manual Codex on the owner's workstation, including Windows or NFS-mounted
local source files, ordinary source-file ACL inheritance, group permissions,
ownership and best-effort file modes are outside the file-at-rest audit scope:
do not block, warn, note or report them. Private copies and mode tightening are
optional; failure to tighten local modes does not stop work. Do not change
original owner-file permissions without authorization. Preserve protection
against actual secret exposure, tampering, remote/protected operations and
explicit security requirements. This exception does not extend to Debian/server,
CI, shared or cloud execution.

## Work within the admitted goal

For Relay product changes that will require a subsequent owner-controlled Apply
after accepted merge, check routine Codex CLI maintenance once per implementation
cycle under the
[CLI maintenance policy](docs/codex/cli-integration.md#relay-development-maintenance-policy).
This applies even when Apply is not a Task completion action and grants no Apply
authority. Compatible bumps belong in the same Task/PR under that standing
authority;
periodic capability review is a separate owner-selected process. This is Relay
development policy, not a downstream consumer requirement.

Use the canonical [progress-bounded execution policy](docs/execution-policy.md)
for correction, stop, prior-state and work-preservation decisions.

For Relay work, default ordinary repository-only implementation or remediation
to automatic execution when its required unprivileged checks are available to
the governed worker. The owner may also authorize the ordinary standalone/manual
route in the Task workflow guide. Manual work is especially useful for required
capabilities unavailable to the worker, protected operations outside disposable
TEST authority, or human judgment or choice. This includes protected root
qualification and live host/environment mutation outside that sandbox.
When implementation and protected/manual qualification are both required to
accept one Task objective, default to one owner-launched manual Codex Step
covering implementation, tests, fixes and disposable or explicitly authorized
qualification before one independent exact-head review. Preserve distinct owner,
source-acceptance, installation, credential and original-attempt native
authorization boundaries. Route selection never expands Task/CR authority or
overrides the progress-bounded execution stops above. An
execution that owns disposable TEST has full operational control over its TEST
effects under the standing
[TEST Environment Authority](docs/execution-policy.md#test-environment-authority).
This can include TEST-specific configuration of shared services when the
execution preserves PROD and other non-TEST users and operates within its
established administrative authority.

For ordinary owner-admitted Relay/Codex work, the default model is
`gpt-6.1-sol`, the default reasoning effort is `xhigh` and the default Subagents
permission is `On`. Explicit live Task or Change Request values override these
defaults; explicit consumer configuration remains owner-controlled. Subagent use
remains discretionary and evidence-driven; permission does not weaken scope,
authority, exact-head, publication, production, credential or protected-boundary
rules. These defaults do not authorize nested Relay execution or retry loops.

## Shared subagent workflow

Relay explicitly adopts the installed passive `org.jresearch.ai/landscape-subagents`
**1.1.0** flow for its own development guidance. When Subagents is On and the
Task and runtime permit delegation, read its complete
[policy](vibevm/vibedeps/org.jresearch.ai.landscape-subagents/1.1.0/vibevm/vibespecs/protocols/subagents.md)
before substantial work. This continues the accepted useful proactive delegation
policy at every supported parent effort, without a helper quota or an Ultra
requirement. Zero helpers remains valid when useful independent work is absent.
The [local binding](docs/codex/SUBAGENTS.md) retains Relay authority and the
migration accounting; the installed flow is the sole reusable policy owner.
Keep the adopted version and admitted profiles stable throughout the Task.
Local Task/CR authority, execution boundaries and Writer/Reviewer separation
override reusable recommendations. Delegation grants no nested Relay execution,
publication, credentials, deployment or independent acceptance authority.
An inner correction does not itself need a new Issue, Step or execution.
A manual task may publish through its explicitly authorized owner channel;
an automatic worker delegates publication to Writer.

## Material User/Operator Contract Change Gate

Apply the complete shared Contract/Decision Maintenance protocol. Relay records
explicit material owner authorization in the live legacy Issue/CR, or the stable
v4 charter and trusted Decision resolved into admission; retained v3 keeps its
complete Request. Unauthorized material behavior is `OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED`
and blocks native approval. Review changed supported Relay commands,
manual/automatic routes, actors, statuses, Outcomes and recovery through
CD-003/004 and the native authority binding.

## Independent review and finding provenance

Before review, read the canonical [review and finding-provenance
contract](reviewer/README.md#independent-review-and-finding-provenance).
Independent native acceptance stays bound to the complete exact head and live
Task/CR authority; implementation helpers and deterministic checks supply evidence.
The material user/operator contract-change gate above remains binding.

## Minimum sufficient ceremony

Follow the [same-Task documentation-maintenance rule](CONTRIBUTING.md#keep-workflow-documentation-current)
when changing human-visible workflows or authority contracts. Use the existing
Task/PR and review; do not introduce a separate documentation approval process.

Use complete shared PC/RA/CD/IR for control proposals, existing proof,
requirement origin, durable decisions and documentation maintenance. Concrete
[Relay control bindings](docs/execution-policy.md#proportional-controls-and-operator-usability)
retain required candidate checks and protected operations.

Wait for required native CI, but leave reconstructible CI/status results in
their native records instead of posting another PASS comment or Outcome update.
Use GH-011 and IR-007/008 to trace requirements, assess completed optional-check
failures and handle unsolicited App suites under the existing review.
If CI fails and the next correction is clear, safe and in scope, correct it and
rerun the relevant validation. Publish material evidence unavailable from those
records, blockers, authority/boundary changes and required handoff information.

Aggregate related findings, use targeted checks while correcting them, and run
the required full candidate set once before handoff unless a later change or
new failure justifies repetition. Close active references when moving an
entrypoint, identifier, shell or execution context. Deterministic PASS does not
replace independent judgment. Keep inner corrections within the admitted goal
and the progress-bounded stops above.

CD-005–007 owns promotion and same-change documentation. Relay executable
Task authority uses its trusted Decision/legacy compatibility mechanisms;
component policy belongs in the existing owning contract.

For all Relay work, read the [product boundaries and validation handoff](vibevm/vibespecs/boot/90-user.md#preserve-the-product-boundaries)
in the project boot lane. They continue this repository's development policy.
